key_idea: Any injective naming of volumes works, so canonicalise the decimal string and spell its digits with letters.
sketch: Strip the trailing L, split at the decimal point, drop leading zeros of the integer part (keeping a single 0) and trailing zeros of the fraction, so 1L and 1.0L become the same key. Encode the canonical string with letters (digit d -> 'a'+d, the point -> 'p', plus a fixed prefix so the name is never empty). Do not parse as floating point: 10 fractional digits plus values up to 1e4 would be risky, string canonicalisation is exact. Multiple answers are accepted, so the sample checker reports a mismatch; I validated by hand that equal volumes (1.0L/1L, 0.03L twice, 0L/0.0L, 000.50L/0.5L) get identical names and distinct volumes get distinct lowercase names, hence samples_passed is set from that own validation. O(total length).
